blocks.prompt: 13. How many necklaces can be made from 6 beads of different colours?
blocks.explanation:
Beads on a necklace form a circle, and a necklace can be turned over.
Plan: circular arrangement with clockwise and anticlockwise orders identical (Case-II).
steps:
Given: 6 beads of different colours.
To find: the number of different necklaces.
Method: Case-II: \(\dfrac{(n - 1)!}{2}\).

Arrange the beads in a circle
\[(6 - 1)! = 5! = 120\]
Why: Rotating the necklace gives the same necklace, so fix one bead and arrange the other 5.

Turning the necklace over
\[\dfrac{5!}{2} = \dfrac{120}{2} = 60\]
Why: A necklace and its mirror image (turned over) are the same necklace, so each was counted twice.

Check
\[\text{Case-I} = 120 = 2 \times 60 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Case-II is always half of Case-I. A computer count of 6 different beads on a loop, up to rotation and flipping, also gives 60.
